title: eDNA Extraction from Water Samples Using NucleoMag DNA/RNA Water Kit
author: Marine Vautier
materials: To limit contamination of the kit buffers, it is recommended to aliquote them: - Into 50 mL tubes for MWA1, MWA2, MWA3 and MWA4 - Into 2 mL tubes for NucleoMag B-Beads solution and DNase-free H 2 O Tubes annotation - one 2 mL tube per sample for lysate collection - one 1.5 mL tube per sample for DNA collection - one 5 mL tube per 8 samples for the NucleoMag B-Beads and MWA2 mix preparation Scissors decontamination (t o be done before starting the protocole, and between each filter cutting) - Prepare : one 50 mL tube with DNA-removing solution (e.g. DNA-off, DNA away) one 50 mL tube with molecular biology grade water one 50 mL tube with ethanol - Successively dip the scissors into each tube, opening and closing the scissors in each tube. Note: The cutting of filters is not a requirement, but it does have an impact on the extraction efficiency.

In this step, the buffers provided by the kit are distributed in a 96-well plate. For DNA extraction from filtered water samples, the 12 columns of the plate are divided into 2 sections of 6 columns each, allowing up to 16 samples to be extracted per plate. Annotate the 96-well plate as recommended below: Table 1: Recommended plaque annotation Note: It is useful to mark the dividing line between columns 6 and 7 with a marker pen to provide a visual cue for filling the plate. Add the appropriate buffers into the appropriate wells of the plate. 1 st column / 7 th column: Will be filled during plate preparation 2/2 2 nd column / 8 th column: 850 µL of MWA3 (1 st wash) 3 rd column / 9 th column: 850 µL of MWA3 (2 nd wash) 4 th column /10 th column: 850 µL of MWA4 (3 rd wash and bead drying) 5 th column / 11 th column: not used 6 th column / 12 th column: 50 µL or 65 µL of DNase-free H 2 O (DNA elution) Note: The choice of elution volume is based on the expected eDNA amount. The smaller the amount, the smaller the elution volume in order to obtain more concentrated DNA. Table 2: Plate preparation 1/2 Film and reserve the plate at Room temperature

steps.title: Prepare MWA2 mix
steps.instruction: Prepare a 5 mL tube (maximum 8 samples) and add only MWA2 buffer; beads will be added later. Include a margin of one sample (e.g., plan mix for 9 samples if extracting 8). Use the volumes indicated in Table 3.

substeps.instruction: Label a 5 mL tube for up to 8 samples.
Add the required volume of MWA2 buffer (see Table 3).
Do not add NucleoMag B‑Beads yet; they will be added during plate preparation.
Prepare mix for one extra sample as a safety margin (e.g., 9 samples for 8 extractions).

steps.title: Lysis of prefilled buffer samples
steps.instruction: Mechanically and chemically lyse filters that already contain buffer, then collect lysate for downstream processing.

substeps.instruction: Collect the 5 mL tubes that contain the filters.
If tubes are frozen, defrost at room temperature for 10 minutes.
Cut the filter into small pieces directly in the tube using decontaminated scissors (decontaminate scissors between samples).
Place the tube on a vertical vortex for 5 seconds at median speed.
Place the tube on a horizontal vortex for 5 seconds at maximum speed.
Transfer the tube to a benchtop centrifuge.
Pipette the lysate from the tube and transfer it into a 2 mL tube.
Centrifuge at 11 000 × g, room temperature, for 30 seconds.
Return the tubes to the rack and keep them at room temperature until distribution into the 96‑well plate.

steps.title: Lysis of samples without buffer
steps.instruction: Mechanically and chemically lyse filters that lack pre‑added buffer, then collect lysate for downstream processing.

substeps.instruction: Collect the 5 mL tubes that contain the filters from the freezer and keep them on ice.
Add 750 µL of MWA1 buffer to each tube immediately.
Cut the filter into small pieces directly in the tube using decontaminated scissors (decontaminate scissors between samples).
Place the tube on a vertical vortex for 5 seconds at median speed.
Place the tube on a horizontal vortex for 5 seconds at maximum speed.
Transfer the tube to a benchtop centrifuge.
Pipette approximately 650 µL of lysate from the tube and transfer it into a 2 mL tube.
Centrifuge at 11 000 × g, room temperature, for 30 seconds.
Return the tubes to the rack and keep them at room temperature until distribution into the 96‑well plate.

steps.title: Prepare bead mix and load plate
steps.instruction: Combine NucleoMag B‑Beads with MWA2 buffer, vortex for homogeneity, and dispense bead‑mix and lysate into the 96‑well plate.

substeps.instruction: Vigorously vortex the NucleoMag B‑Beads tube.
For each tube containing MWA2 buffer (prepared earlier), add the appropriate volume of NucleoMag B‑Beads as specified in Table 3.
Vortex the resulting NucleoMag B‑Beads + MWA2 mixture to ensure homogeneity; vortex between samples if needed.
Remove the film from the 96‑well plate.
Add 500 µL of the NucleoMag B‑Beads + MWA2 mix to each well of column 1 and column 7.
Add 450 µL of lysate supernatant (from the 2 mL tubes) to the same wells, following the layout described in Table 4.

steps.title: Run extraction on MagnetaPure
steps.instruction: Execute the DNA/RNA extraction program on the MagnetaPure 32 system using the prepared plate.

substeps.instruction: Place the plate into the MagnetaPure 32 system and insert the magnetic rod cover.
Select the appropriate program for the desired elution volume and temperature (see Table 5).
Note: Elution at 56 °C can increase DNA yield but may cause evaporation, reducing final volume.
Start the run (approximately 40 minutes).

steps.title: Post‑run DNA handling
steps.instruction: Collect the eluates, decontaminate equipment, and store DNA extracts appropriately.

substeps.instruction: Remove the plate from the instrument and place it into the DNA‑workstation.
Remove the magnetic rod cover and initiate UV decontamination as described in the instrument manual.
Transfer each DNA extract into a pre‑annotated 1.5 mL tube.
Optionally measure DNA concentration and quality (e.g., using a Nanodrop).
Store DNA extracts at 4 °C for immediate use, or at –20 °C / –80 °C for long‑term preservation.
